correctness.rationale: Two omissions in a clique fiber have the same selected neighbors, so neither could have a private witness. With at most one omission per fiber and m≥2, every fiber contains a selected vertex. Its selected vertices see exactly the omissions indexed by the intersection of the base closed neighborhood with U. The private-witness test is therefore precisely irredundance, in both directions. Each support lifts m^|U| ways; strict extensions of an omitted set are possible exactly when its base support extends (keeping existing omissions). This proves the polynomial and distinguishes maximal supports for inclusion-minimal D from largest supports for minimum-cardinality D. On cycles, 111 kills a center's witness, and 1101 or its reflection kills a doubleton endpoint's outward witness as well as its self and inward options. Conversely a singleton witnesses itself and a doubleton endpoint has an outward zero whose other neighbor is zero. This is the intended reading at line 54, not that both neighbors of the outward zero are absent. The cyclic factor test wraps correctly at n=3. In the trace, the indexed appended bits specify a unique closed walk, including for periodic words. For k ones and q doubletons there are k−q gaps; with both types present and c cyclic blocks of consecutive doubletons, q+c distinct gaps need an extra zero beyond one per gap. At even maximum density no mixed case is possible, leaving only alternation and, if 4 divides n, four rotations of 1100. At odd maximum density a mixed case has c=1 and all gaps forced; in the pure cases exactly one gap takes the spare zero. For each allowable doubleton count 0 through floor(k/2), a unique marked boundary can occur at any of the n positions. This gives n floor((n+3)/4) and the stated lift factor. The m≥2 boundary is real: for m=1 over K1 the singleton support is irredundant but omitting its sole vertex gives no selected witness.
residual_risks: Finite replay is bounded; the general graph witness translation and the cyclic gap argument establish the full claim. The formula counts minimum-cardinality sets, not all inclusion-minimal sets; it assumes clique fibers, m≥2, and labeled cycles.

originality.rationale: Credit the configuration-level correspondence between all super dominating complements of a genuine clique blowup and all irredundant supports in an arbitrary base graph, including the weighted polynomial transform and the maximal-support refinement. Do not credit the existence of a super-domination polynomial, the unweighted base-cycle data or product cardinality bounds as new. The most relevant inspected product statements concern optimal cardinality or restrictions on minimum sets; the available catalogue and primary evidence does not establish the full correspondence. The directly relevant Kaidash chapter remains an explicit access risk, not a negative finding about its contents.
residual_risks: Kaidash's full chapter remains unavailable; neither its examples nor any general clique-product theorem were inspected. The 1979 Bollobás–Cockayne irredundance paper was not retrieved for cycle-specific comparison. A failed lookup, irrelevant web results, and keyword misses do not exclude equivalent prior work.

value.rationale: A scalar product bound cannot tell which selections are feasible or how many have a given size. The exact correspondence makes the entire super-domination enumerator of a natural graph product accessible from a different standard base-graph invariant, and it determines the inclusion-minimal configurations without a separate blowup search. The worked cycle case shows how an established base family becomes a weighted exact invariant on a larger graph. This is useful even though the witness argument is short and the underlying base-cycle data are known.
residual_risks: Value rests on the all-configuration translation, not on rediscovering base-cycle sequences or on generic transfer-matrix machinery. No efficient algorithm is claimed for enumerating irredundance on arbitrary base graphs.
